text:
sara_support: FYI incoming escal on #12345 — user in EU reports lots of 401s starting ~08:12 UTC and unusually high egress/billing. They say requests are going to us-west despite region pinned to eu-central. Can infra take a look?

kevin_infra: On it. Any recent policy changes?

sara_support: Support notes: customer updated a failover policy via UI at 07:58 (small reorder), attached screenshot in ticket. They also saw latency spike when the misroute happened.

mike_oncall: pulling logs for that tenant now. Give me the API key id or example request ts.

sara_support: example request id: req_0a3f7c, API key ends with -eu. Ticket includes curl sample that fails.

kevin_infra: seeing a config change around 07:58 from deploy-bot (UI change). The failover array was saved as: ["us-west-2", "eu-central-1"] but customer expected ["eu-central-1", "us-west-2"]. Looks like the UI sort routine put regions in lexical order when weights were omitted.

lisa_prod: oof — so priority index got shifted because they didn't set explicit priority/weight. That would cause sticky routing to prefer us-west as failover primary. Explains auth 401 since tokens scoped to eu region.

mike_oncall: grabbing traces now. Repro: curl \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" -H \"X-Client-Region: eu-central-1\" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

deploy-bot: change_record: user=sara_support_ui id=cfg_9876 action=update fields=[failover_regions] at=2025-03-06T07:58:12Z

kevin_infra: I can reproduce locally by using the policy JSON without weights: 

```json
{
  "failover_regions": ["eu-central-1","us-west-2"]
}
```
When the UI saved it, client-side normalization sorted array to ["us-west-2","eu-central-1"] if weights missing. Routing evaluation uses array order as priority.

sara_support: customer billing noticed spike because cross-region egress priced higher. They're annoyed. Anna from billing pinged me.

anna_billing: saw a billing jump tied to tenant id t-339, egress to us-west increased ~4x between 08:12-08:34 UTC. Will hold charge pending root cause.

kevin_infra: immediate mitigation: revert config to previous commit: set explicit priority order and pin region. I'll push a patch to treat empty weights as "preserve order" instead of normalize-sort.

mike_oncall: temp mitigation for the tenant: applied region pinning on their API key (force routing to eu) and cleared KV cache of routing results. Confirmed requests now land in eu-central and 401s stop.

lisa_prod: longer term: UI fix + server-side validation to disallow silent reorder when weights absent, and a post-deploy smoke test for auth-scoped keys. Also add a warning in the UI: "Omitting explicit failover weights may change priority order".

kevin_infra: created PR #8021 with server-side guard and a migration to detect other policies saved with implicit reorder. Rolling to prod in next window.

sara_support: customer updated ticket asking for timeline + request for credit. I told them rollback applied and working; will follow up with RCA. Thanks everyone. :pray:

mike_oncall: marking incident:region-mispriority-2141599999, will attach logs + a reproduction script in the ticket.

kevin_infra: reproduction script (use with a test API key):

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/route-check \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-test-eu\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"policy": {"failover_regions": ["eu-central-1","us-west-2"]}}' | jq
```

sara_support: copying resolution notes to customer and adding billing contact. Closing here once billing confirms. :white_check_mark:
